cat > /tmp/pr-body.md <<'MDEOF'
The Paper file's five console screens, and the API work they needed. Six
commits, each one landing its own lanes, gates, and doc rows.

## The counter route could never answer

`crates/cachet-worker/src/api.rs:142` reads
`env.var("CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID")` on every request and the alchemy
program never bound it, so `GET /api/self/events` answered 503
`storage_unavailable` on every deployment, including one configured with
a stats token. The counting worked; the reporting had not run once since
the route shipped in #24.

Nobody noticed because the route's success path had no test coverage of
any kind. `workerd/wrangler.toml` bound no Analytics Engine dataset and
set no token, so all six lane rows were refused at the config check
before any query ran, and `stats::emit` returned early in every scenario.
`run_stats_sql`, the row deserialization, the response shaping, and the
whole writer path were untested.

Both halves are fixed. `loadStageConfig` now refuses a stats token that
arrives without an account id, because half a credential is a chart that
never loads rather than an error anyone sees. The lane's stub server
gained a fourth role, Cloudflare's SQL API, reached through a new
`CACHET_STATS_API_URL` seam the way the JWKS and GitHub API are already
reached through theirs. It receives the composed statement as text, so
the lane asserts it whole rather than by substring: this statement runs
with an account token behind it.

## What the screens needed

`by=hour` and `by=day` group into time buckets and answer a series:
oldest first, one row per bucket, zeros included, each dimension the
bucket's first instant in epoch seconds. A bucket finer than its window
can hold is refused rather than truncated, because a truncated series is
a chart that silently starts partway through its own window. `kind`,
`outcome`, and `actor` narrow an answer to one value each, which is what
makes "laptop reads by outcome" askable.

Filters meant the writer's vocabulary had to close: `StatKind` and
`StatOutcome` replace the free strings, so a filter value parses into the
same set the writers emit before anything is formatted into SQL. One test
now ties the two sides together where a comment used to name the risk.

Three more things that surfaced on the way. Writes never measured their
bytes, so "pushed this week" had no source. The multipart open and
completion branches returned past the counter, so `begin` and `complete`
were kinds the router named and no point ever carried. And `by=project`
could only ever answer one empty row, because nothing had ever filled
`blob6`.

`GET /api/whoami` answers who a request authenticates as, admin or not: a
console that could only learn its standing by provoking a 403 would make
a refusal part of loading a page. `GET /api/self/health` answers the
console header's status and countdown.

## A browser session could read the cache

`read_routes` authorized narinfo and NAR reads through `authorize_read`,
which accepts the session cookie and answers `ReadIdentity::Session` with
no scope attached. `resolve_session` never re-checks org membership, so a
copy of an ex-member's cookie substituted from the cache for up to a
fortnight after they left.

Sessions are see-only now: they authenticate the console's own surface
and answer 401 on the paths that serve cache bytes. Nix reads through a
netrc and never sends a cookie, so nothing that reads for real loses a
credential. ADR 0016 records the scope and names the fourteen-day counter
window as an accepted trade rather than leaving the threat model claiming
a re-check the code never performed.

## Serving the console

Assets mount under `/console` on the worker's own deployment, and the
root redirects there. Same origin is what makes the session cookie work
at all: it is `SameSite=Lax` on `Path=/`, and the worker emits no
`Access-Control-*` headers.

Both of the asset layer's handling modes are off, and that is the whole
safety argument. A binary cache is read by asking about paths that mostly
are not in it, and nix reads a 404 as "ask the next substituter". A layer
answering an unmatched request with an application shell turns every
cache miss into `200 text/html`.

`run_worker_first: true` was the first answer and it was wrong: it puts
the worker in front of `/cdn-cgi/*`, which the platform and the local
runner reserve, and it broke the collector's dev endpoint immediately.
ADR 0014 records that.

## The console

Five screens: what the cache holds and what pushed it, what the collector
has been doing, who can reach the deployment, the traffic it serves, and
what it does for people rather than for CI. It reads and never writes.

React with TanStack Router and Query, StyleX against the tokens carried
over from the design, and hand-drawn SVG for the charts. Every answer
decodes through an `effect` schema before a screen sees it, so a
deployment newer or older than the console beside it fails at the
boundary with the field named rather than three components later as an
`undefined` on screen.

The states the mockups do not draw are the ones a real deployment
reaches, and each says what is true instead of showing an error: signed
out, an org member who is not an admin, a deployment that has never
collected, and one counting without a token to report with.

## Two bugs found by running it rather than by testing it

StyleX compiles longhands, so `background: "none"` was dropped and every
button fell back to the user agent's light default. And the bars' track
and fill were spans, which are inline, so neither the height nor the
width applied and every row rendered as the same full-width strip.

## A lane bug, not a flake

The push payload was `cachet workerd lane payload <pid>`, and the
operating system recycles pids. A run that drew one an earlier run had
already pushed found its path in the store snapshot, uploaded nothing,
minted no token, and failed three checks at once with nothing in any
message to say why. Three such paths were sitting in a dev machine's
store. The content is a uuid now, and the mint assertions carry the count
they actually saw.

Two more caught by tests rather than by luck: the property lane found an
epoch boundary where the series window ran off the front and ended in the
future, and the console's schema test caught a mirror in `cachet-api`
carrying `skip_serializing_if` on a field the core type writes as `null`,
so the generated document promised an absent key for one that is always
present. That mirror test now compares serializations rather than fields.

## Gates

A new lane, `console`, with its row in `lanes.toml`, its doc, its verb,
and its CI job. `just check` passes, the workerd lane is green with a new
scenario for the console's routing law, and the integration lane gains
three steps: the root redirects, the shell serves and names a script the
build emitted, and an absent narinfo still answers 404 and not HTML.

ADRs 0014, 0015, and 0016. `docs/console.md` joins the §11 manifest.

content.text:
No, and both of its settings are now traps.

**As an override** (`CACHET_DEPLOY_UI_ORIGIN=https://ui.example.com`) it redirects the browser to a UI that structurally cannot authenticate. The session cookie is `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/` on the deployment's host, the worker emits no `Access-Control-*` headers, and it answers `OPTIONS` with a 404. So the person lands on that origin with no credential and no way to acquire one. The redirect works; nothing after it does.

**As an off switch** (`CACHET_DEPLOY_UI_ORIGIN=""`) it answers 204 instead of redirecting, but it doesn't disable anything. No. Creating the environment changes nothing about the automatic path.

The `workflow_run` trigger only ever reaches the `staging` job, and that job is doubly hardcoded: `environment: staging` on line 36, `just deploy cachet-staging` on line 66. Neither reads `inputs.stage`, because on a `workflow_run` event there are no inputs. Production can only be reached through `manual` (line 99), which is gated on `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` — a button press.

So creating a `production` environment does exactly one thing: makes the dispatch path work instead of failing at config load. And if you put a required-reviewer rule on it, the dispatched run parks and waits for your approval before any step executes, which is the gate DEPLOY.md describes.

Worth knowing about the concurrency group on line 27: it keys on `inputs.stage` for a dispatch and `cachet-staging` otherwise, so a production deploy and a staging deploy occupy different slots and never queue behind each other.

The one sharp edge is that `manual` accepts `cachet-staging` too, and then resolves to the `staging` environment — so the same environment's secrets serve both a hand-triggered staging deploy and the automatic one. That's deliberate and fine; it just means production is the only stage whose secrets would live somewhere new.

Confirmed, and it's a second half of the same bug I only half-fixed.

`CACHET_SIGNING_KEY` and `CACHET_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` are set **bare** in the workflow env, and `Config.redacted` reads those bare names — consistent. The stats token isn't: the workflow and your secrets and DEPLOY.md all use the prefixed `CACHET_DEPLOY_STATS_TOKEN`, `loadStageConfig` reads that prefixed name for the *condition*, and then `infra/alchemy.run.ts:77` binds `Config.redacted("CACHET_STATS_TOKEN")` — the **bare** name, which nothing sets.

So the condition passes and alchemy then looks up a variable that isn't in the environment. Either it fails the deploy or it binds an empty secret; either way the token never reaches the worker. This shipped with #24 next to the account-id bug — I fixed that half and didn't check this one.

Config.redacted("CACHET_STATS_TOKEN")  ->  Config.redacted("CACHET_DEPLOY_STATS_TOKEN")
